predecessors.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
predecessors.text: Yemen, where the last Ayyubid al-Malik al-Mas'ud 'left Yemen in 1229' and handed governance to his commander

successors.name: Tahirid Sultanate
successors.text: the Tihama lowland and the southern highlands, with Aden

successors.name: Kathiri Sultanate
successors.text: Shihr in Hadramawt, taken by the Tahirids in 1457 and lost 'at the end of the fifteenth century to the Kathiri princedom' (Tahirid page)

ledger.x: 1229: Umar takes over the government of Yemen when the last Ayyubid al-Mas'ud leaves, the start of the Rasulid dynasty.
1350: Mecca passes out of Rasulid reach (bridging).
1443: Lahij falls to the Tahir clan.
1454: the last Rasulid sultan gives up the throne to the Tahirids and the dynasty ends.

wars.name: Rasulid-Zaydi struggle for Sanaa and the highlands
wars.outcome: Under Yusuf I the Rasulids 'temporarily occupied' Sanaa and defeated the imams several times; the Zaidis regained ground in the highlands from the late 13th century and took Sanaa in 1324.

wars.name: Capture of al-Mujahid Ali at Mecca
wars.outcome: 'In 1350 the Rasulid sultan al-Mujahid Ali was captured by Egyptian Mamluks in Mecca when he went on a pilgrimage.'

wars.name: Tahirid takeover of the Rasulid realm
wars.outcome: Lahij fell to the Tahir clan in 1443 and Aden in 1454; al-Mas'ud gave up the throne to az-Zafir Amir bin Tahir in 1454 and 'The new ruling clan governed Yemen from 1454 to 1517 as the Tahirids'.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line.
